focus: /doctor:git router contract, ownership boundary, placement decision, rejected designs, battery composition
answeredQuestions: Does the sk-git setup belong in /doctor:git as a new action or in a separate command, and which ideas should be rejected?

label: /doctor:git is a mandatory-gate thin router; _routes.yaml canonical manifest carries target/yaml/setup_vars/allowed_flags/mutating/gate3_location/mcp_tools/script_invocations/trigger_phrases; new target = one route + one doctor-*.yaml asset + command listing

Existing hooks+standards routes are mutating but their script_invocations already enumerate the check-only calls a setup battery reuses: git-hook-gates list --json, install-git-hooks.sh --status, git-standards status|check --json, validate-message --explain

Precedent route shape verbatim: /doctor:sk-code setup is mutating:read-only, gate3_location n/a, one script invocation; workflow YAML = single-step read_only, approvals none, forbidden_targets all, repair-is-explicit-operator-action invariant, exit 0/1/2 -> STATUS=OK/FAIL/ERROR

Placement decision: setup belongs in /doctor:git as a third read-only target — owner match (skill_agent: sk-git), repair adjacency (repairs are the same command's hooks/standards or git config), precedent, and discoverability via list/?

Rejected: R1 separate /doctor:sk-git (doubles router, wrong concern name); R2 flag on hooks/standards (read-only battery violates mutates class); R3 /doctor:git-setup (breaks command-target grammar); R4 mutating setup (violates read-only-diagnostic invariant); R5 per-tool --doctor flags (scatters battery); R6 --status alone (hook resolution only)

Ownership boundary has three classes: (a) repo-owned config (.sk-git/, skgit.contractDir, speckit.hooks.*, skilled.trustRepoHooks, skilled.commitId, speckit.worktreeBase, env suppressions, .git/hooks foreign hooks); (b) vendored-skill files (allowlist resolves at repo toplevel .skilled/.opencode copy, provision-paths beside script, hard-rules.json beside SKILL.md — no second override layer); (c) runtime-registered adapters
hard-rules.json silent-failure mode: evaluate() skips rules whose check name is not in the registry ('unknown check -> skip'); a read-only leg can prove every rule.check is in GIT_CHECKS

Proposed 11-leg battery: provisioning, hook install status, trust, gates registry, standards check, contractDir validity, allowlist parse, worktree base+provision paths, Commit-Id opt-in+allocator, advisory rule-key resolution, suppression audit

Non-vendored consumers customize only class (a); allowlist/provision-paths/hard-rules/gates.tsv are shared-install files whose edits affect every repo — the check must report shared scope, not invite repo edits

Residual unknowns: (u1) no uniform probe for per-runtime adapter registration -> SKIP with file paths; (u2) no repo-local hard-rules.json overlay found; (u3) Spec trailer semantics for non-specs repos rely on .sk-git rules override not a dedicated switch
